gap: No result ChatGPT got states battery energy per pound: the Samsung Galaxy Tab Active5 Pro carries about 25.0 Wh/lb (two 3.85 V packs rated 4,900 mAh each, 37.7 Wh, in 683 g). The Panasonic TOUGHBOOK G2 mk3 carries 23.4 Wh/lb with the 68 Wh battery and 18.9 Wh/lb with the 50 Wh one. The Dell Pro Rugged 12 at its $3,498 base price carries 12.3 Wh/lb, because that price includes only one of its two 35.6 Wh packs. The second pack costs $30 more.
standout_why: I compared against the two Panasonic pages ChatGPT cited. The US TOUGHBOOK G2 page gives '15 hours - Mobile Mark 2025' and 2.9 lb but no Wh figure. The EU/CH G2 page gives 50 Wh and 68 Wh with weights of 2.64 lb and 2.9 lb but no Wh-per-lb figure, and it covers no other brand. Neither page has Samsung or Dell battery energy. Neither notes that the $3,498 Dell base configuration ships with one 35.6 Wh pack and that the second costs $30. I could not read the top third-party results: rottenwifi.com timed out and then returned 502, and itechguides.com returned 502. So I can't rule out that one of them states part of this, and that is why the score is 2 and not 3.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's 'best value for Android' pick on a figure it never stated: the Active5 Pro carries the most battery energy per pound of the candidates I could source, and its packs are removable. For a Windows buyer it changes the Dell advice: the $3,498 configuration ChatGPT showed has half the tablet's battery capacity, so the shopper should add the $30 second 35.6 Wh pack. That brings it to 71.2 Wh for $3,528, which is $49.6 per Wh against $98.3 per Wh for the base configuration. With the 68 Wh battery, the Panasonic G2 mk3 is close behind Samsung at 23.4 Wh/lb, with an official 15 h MobileMark 25 runtime.
